disease_label_per_paper: Hypertensive emergency as initial presentation of systemic sclerosis sine scleroderma
presentation_summary: A 53-year-old African American woman with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, morbid obesity, and CKD stage 3 presented with progressive shortness of breath.

Initial evaluation showed BP 253/122 mmHg, HR 81/min, RR 24/min, and oxygen saturation 80%. She was awake but in significant respiratory distress with bilateral extremity edema and bibasilar crackles.
She had no rash, joint pain, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, hair loss, dysphagia, Raynaud phenomenon, or skin tightening.
She was admitted to the ICU with hypertensive emergency, acute hypoxic and hypercarbic respiratory failure, acute on chronic renal failure, and acute pulmonary edema.

Labs included creatinine 3.32 mg/dL, BNP 429 pg/mL, pH 7.19, pCO2 53, hemoglobin 6.9 g/dL, platelets 177 x10^9/L, ANA 1:640 homogeneous positive, anti-Scl-70 positive, RNA polymerase III IgG weakly positive at 31.6 U, and normal C3/C4.

There was no evidence of MAHA: LDH and bilirubin were normal and no schistocytes were seen on smear. Urinalysis showed small blood, 41-50 WBC per high-power field, and urine protein/creatinine ratio 9.5.
Renal ultrasound showed normal-sized non-echogenic kidneys, and echocardiogram showed mild LVH with preserved ejection fraction.

SRC sine scleroderma was diagnosed based on severe uncontrolled hypertension, worsening renal failure, positive anti-Scl-70 and RNA polymerase III antibodies, and absence of cutaneous/digital findings.

Captopril was started at 6.25 mg TID and titrated to 12.5 mg TID, but BP remained difficult to control despite multiple vasodilators and kidney function did not recover; she developed end-stage kidney failure and hemodialysis was started.

quality_warnings: This case lacks MAHA despite SRC; absence of schistocytes, normal LDH, normal bilirubin, and normal platelet count are retained rather than removed.
Sine scleroderma context is represented by absent skin/Raynaud/dysphagia findings plus positive serology; the disease name remains Systemic sclerosis renal crisis.
No unreported BUN value, renin value, renal biopsy result, or exact follow-up creatinine was fabricated.
